LET’S GET CONNECTED

Your guitar. Meet Voltage.

  1. Plug into an audio interface.

    Connect your guitar to a USB audio interface’s instrument/Hi-Z input, then plug the interface into your computer. A guitar needs an instrument input; a simple cable into a headphone jack won’t do the job.

  2. Connect wired headphones.

    Use the interface’s headphone output. Turn off its direct monitoring so you only hear the processed tone. Start with low hardware gain and volume.

  3. Power up and choose your input.

    Click Connect guitar, allow audio input access, then select your interface and the channel your guitar uses. Play hard and keep the input meter below clipping.

For the best response, use Chrome or Edge and wired headphones. Bluetooth adds delay. Browser and driver latency varies; Voltage cannot select an ASIO driver.
AUDIO SETTINGS

Fine-tune your connection.

Use your system sound settings if output selection is unavailable.

Connect your guitar to see the sample rate and estimated output latency.

Recordings use your browser's supported audio format (usually WebM/Opus), with a 30-minute limit. Download before leaving. Presets stay in this browser; custom cabinet IRs and loops are session-only. Greenback and Vintage 30 use measured cabinet responses; the other built-in cabinets use speaker-style filters.

Shortcuts: M mute output · T tuner.
